To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified miRNAs that regulate key players in the IL-6 signal pathway and have shown that IL-6 has only minor effects on the miRNAome of hepatoma cells.

IL-6 and hyperIL-6 have differential effects on the miRNA expression of hepatoma cell lines and primary human hepatocytes, which is in part dependent on the cell type; miR-146a and miR-146c are the most prominent miRNAs regulating STAT3, and miR-21 regulates STAT1.
1. IL-6 has a profound effect of the transcriptome of hepatoma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of miRNAs involved in the IL-6 signaling pathway and their relevance for liver diseases.
the elucidation of miRNA-mediated regulation of IL-6 signalling and with the analysis of miRNA expression in HCC and NASH.
the identification of regulatory mechanisms that contribute to the pathogenesis of chronic liver diseases and may be exploited for therapeutic interventions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miR-146a/b is the most prominent miRNA that is induced by IL-6.
IL-6 has a profound effect not only on the transcriptome but also on the miRnome, and that this may be of relevance for the development and progression of liver diseases.
IL-6 induces a differential regulation of thousands genes in hepatoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-6 has profound effects on the transcriptome of hepatoma cells but only few miRNAs change significantly.
IL-6 has only limited effects on the miRNAome, while IFN-g has profound effects.
IL-6 has a limited effect on the miRNA expression in hepatocytes and hepatoma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-6 induces the regulation of only a limited number of miRNAs in the investigated hepatoma cell lines and that these miRNAs may contribute to the regulation of the IL-6 signalling pathway.
the IL-6-induced differential regulation of thousands mRNAs is accompanied by the differential regulation of only selected miRNas.
the effects of IL6 on the miRNAs are rather small compared to the effects of IFN-γ.
